newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Alliance Imaging sees Q1 EPS up.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Alliance Imaging sees Q1 EPS up.

text.p: Alliance Imaging Inc expects to report first quarter operating earnings of $0.14 a share, up from $0.10 a year earlier, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Richard Zehner said in a recent interview.
The rise will reflect improved profit margins, higher demand for the company's magnetic resonance imaging services, and the acquisition of new MRI machines, he told Reuters.
Revenues for the first quarter are expected to exceed $19 million, up from $14.7 million in the comparable 1996 period, Zehner said.
Alliance Imaging will have about $0.26 a share of extraordinary gains in the first quarter from repurchasing preferred stock at a discount and from refinancing transactions, he said.

"The industry is going through a very nice growth phase," Zehner said. Although an increasingly cost-conscious health care environment has driven down the cost of MRI procedures, this has been offset by improved MRI technology, which has increased demand for the procedure for a broader range of uses, he said.

MRI machines have traditionally been used to scan for lesions or tumors in the brain or to detect knee or shoulder injuries. Newer machines can pick up subtle irregularities in breast and prostate tissue and in blood vessels.
"We took a very aggressive stance replacing the less sophisticated machines. Now we are at the end of the replacement cycle and we're getting growth from more advanced scanners," Zehner said.

Although the cost of an MRI scan has dropped to around $600 from $1,700 in 1990, Alliance's operating profit margins are "as high as they've ever been," approaching 55 percent in the 1997 first quarter, up from 51 percent a year ago, he said.
The company did about 40,000 MRI procedures in the first quarter, up from 30,000 a year earlier.
Growth will come from the addition of new machines internally, and through acquisitions, he said. "The industry is highly fragmented. There is tremendous consolidation opportunity."

Although it is one of the dominant players in the industry, Alliance Imaging currently operates just 90 of the 3,600 MRI machines in operation. Zehner said it will add at least 15 machines this year, plus an unspecified number through acquisitions.
